contracts: One verb per DOMAIN_MAP tool in AREAS; positional args for required params, --flags for optional ones; dict params take a JSON string through cli.json_object
A verb's mode is 'write' if and only if (area, action) is in the hand-reviewed WRITE table; nothing is inferred

A verb passes the handler only the arguments the user supplied: optional flags default to argparse.SUPPRESS and the call is `call(area, action, **given(ns, <handler param names>))`, so the handler's own defaults apply (task:2cea5538)
A handler's `limit` is fed from the global --limit only when it was passed (given drops None)
Generated modules import only from mac.groups._backend (call, given) plus argparse and cli.json_object when needed; handlers still load lazily through dispatcher.resolve
generated-group-verbs.description: Dev-time generator that writes mac/groups/<area>.py for the simple local-mac groups from DOMAIN_MAP and each handler's inspect.signature. The generated modules are committed so `mac` never imports handlers just to build its parser.
invariants: Committed mac/groups/<area>.py must equal render() output for the current handlers; CoverageTest.test_generated_modules_are_current fails otherwise
tests/test_parity_simple_groups.py keeps its own copy of WRITE, so a mode change needs both edits
Generated modules contain no copied handler default values; a handler-side default change reaches `mac` without regeneration
CLI rows in mcp_tool_calls log only supplied args (e.g. '{}'), so they differ in shape from MCP rows, which carry FastMCP-filled defaults; nothing reads args_json

Hand-written mac/groups/notes.py and reminders.py are outside the generator but follow the same rule by hand: SUPPRESS defaults plus given(), no copied handler defaults (task:906b962e); ForwardingTest in tests/test_parity_notes_reminders.py pins exact kwargs
generated-group-verbs.name: generated-group-verbs

contracts: tools(name) imports tools.<name> from MAC_MCP_SRC or ~/workspace/claude_for_mac_local/src; a missing tree raises Failure('backend_missing')
call(handler, **kw) turns a raised ValueError/RuntimeError or an {'error': ...} result into Failure('tool_error')
call() returns [] for the handlers' 'No ... found.' sentinel strings; any other result passes through unchanged

call(area, action, /, **kw) resolves the handler via dispatcher.resolve (DOMAIN_MAP) and runs it via dispatcher.invoke, so the call is logged to mcp_tool_calls and passes the same gates as the MCP tool

tool_hooks.Refused becomes Failure('blocked'); a raised ValueError/RuntimeError or an {'error': ...} result becomes Failure('tool_error'); other exceptions (including an OS PermissionError) reach cli.py as Failure('internal')
A missing source tree (MAC_MCP_SRC or ~/workspace/claude_for_mac_local/src) or an unimportable dispatcher/tool_hooks raises Failure('backend_missing') — the call never runs without the gates
Results pass through unchanged; handlers return [] for empty results
mcp-handler-backend.description: Adapter that runs local-mac MCP tool handlers through local-mac's own dispatcher (resolve + invoke) and maps their results onto the mac JSON/error/exit-code contract. Group modules call handlers only through call(area, action, **kwargs).
invariants: The MCP handler stays the single implementation; verbs never re-implement AppleScript
Modules prefixed '_' under mac/groups are not loaded as verb groups by registry.load_groups
The MCP handler stays the single implementation and DOMAIN_MAP the single routing table; verbs never re-implement AppleScript or copy the area→module mapping
Offline tests stub _backend.dispatcher; HookTest uses the real invoke with only resolve stubbed and a scratch DB
mcp-handler-backend.name: mcp-handler-backend
